verdict.rationale: SigNoz documents filtering traces by any span attribute, querying logs in List, Time Series and Table views, breaking panels out by an attribute, and running ClickHouse SQL. Together these imply ad-hoc filter and group-by on arbitrary attributes without pre-aggregation. However, nothing addresses high-cardinality fields like user or request IDs. A community report also found that querying attributes stored as maps was 10-50x slower than regular columns, which suggests performance depends on schema or column promotion. missing for 10: explicit documentation of high-cardinality group-by (user id, request id), confirmation that no index or column definition is needed for good performance, independent hands-on corroboration.
